newsitem.title: OMAN: Maersk joins Oman Salalah port service co.
newsitem.headline: Maersk joins Oman Salalah port service co.

text.p: Maersk line has acquired a 15 percent stake in Oman's Salalah Port Services Company (SPS), a company being formed to develop the Gulf state's port of Mina Raysut, an SPS statement said on Monday.

"An agreement was signed this morning which introduces and adds Maersk as one of the founder shareholders with a 15 percent stake," the statement said, adding that the move would result in Maersk bringing "a significant volume of cargo" to Mina Raysut.
Maersk Line is owned by Denmark's A.P. Moeller shipping group.
"Maersk operates a global container network in alliance with Sea-Land, and Mina Raysut will, from mid-1998 be called by the joint service network of the two carriers," the statement added.
SPS other founder shareholders are Oman's government, CSX Corp's Sea-Land Services, local firms and pension funds.
Oman said in October the government is investing $140 million in the project and that 20 percent of the company's shares would be offered for public subscription
Oman hopes Mina Raysut will establish it as a gateway for container traffic in the Gulf, east Africa and India.
Mina Raysut's masterplan calls for the development of more than 10 berths and dry dock facilities.
